name: Introduction and overview — AH-64 Apache — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — AH-64 Apache
description: Introduction and overview of the AH-64 Apache: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The AH-64 Apache is a twin-engine attack helicopter built by Hughes (now Boeing), entering service in 1986. It carries Hellfire missiles, rockets, and a 30 mm chain gun slaved to the gunner's helmet sight. About 2,400 have been built; the Apache became the U.S. Army's primary attack helicopter and serves with many allied nations. Baseline facts: Twin-engine attack helicopter; service from 1986; ~2,400 built by Hughes/Boeing..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
